name: Ash Kalra
title: California State Assemblymember, Chair of the Assembly Committee on Judiciary
district: California State Assembly District 25 (San José and southeast Santa Clara County; represented District 27 from 2016–2022 before redistricting)
years_of_service: December 5, 2016–present (currently serving his fifth term, re-elected November 2024).
background: Kalra was born January 21, 1972, in Toronto to Punjabi parents from India; his family immigrated to the United States in 1978 and settled in San Jose, where he graduated from Oak Grove High School. He earned a B.A. in Communications from UC Santa Barbara in 1993 and a J.D. from Georgetown University in 1996, teaching at inner-city Washington, D.C. schools while in law school. He is the first Hindu and first Indian American to serve in the California Legislature. (Source: official Assembly biography, a25.asmdc.org; Wikipedia, Ash Kalra.)

Before elected office, Kalra worked for 11 years as a Deputy Public Defender for Santa Clara County, representing indigent clients in felony and misdemeanor cases with a focus on drug treatment court and rehabilitation advocacy. He also taught law at San Jose State University and Lincoln Law School of San José. He served on the San José City Council representing District 2 from January 6, 2009 to December 5, 2016 before being elected to the Assembly. (Source: official Assembly biography, a25.asmdc.org.)

Kalra was first elected to the Assembly in November 2016, defeating fellow Democrat Madison Nguyen 53.2%–46.8% in the general election for the open District 27 seat, after placing second to Nguyen in a seven-candidate June 2016 primary. He was re-elected in 2018 (76.3%) and 2020 (72.6%) against Republican G. Burt Lancaster, and after 2021 redistricting moved his seat to District 25, in 2022 (70.0%) and 2024 (68.4%) against Republican Ted Stroll. He chairs the Assembly Committee on Judiciary and previously chaired the Assembly Labor and Employment Committee and the Assembly Select Committee on the Future of Work and Workers; he also chairs the California Legislative Progressive Caucus. (Source: Wikipedia, Ash Kalra (Ballotpedia unreachable — see note below); official Assembly biography.)

voting_record_highlights: AB 2542 (2019–2020), the California Racial Justice Act, prohibiting the seeking or obtaining of criminal convictions or sentences on the basis of race, ethnicity, or national origin: Kalra was the lead Assembly author (with Kamlager, Robert Rivas, and Santiago; Bradford and Mitchell in the Senate). It passed the Senate concurrence vote 49–16 on August 31, 2020, and was signed by Gov. Gavin Newsom on September 30, 2020 as Chapter 317, Statutes of 2020. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for AB 2542.)

AB 1947 (2019–2020), extending the time workers have to file retaliation/whistleblower complaints with the Labor Commissioner from six months to one year and allowing attorney's fees for successful whistleblower plaintiffs: Kalra was a lead author with Lorena Gonzalez. It passed the Senate floor vote 28–12 on August 24, 2020, and was signed September 30, 2020 as Chapter 344, Statutes of 2020. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for AB 1947.)

AB 1400 (2021–2022), the CalCare Act, which would have created a single-payer universal health care system in California: Kalra was the lead author (with Lee and Santiago). It passed the Assembly Appropriations Committee 11–3 on January 20, 2022, but Kalra himself pulled it from consideration and it died on the Assembly floor without a vote on February 1, 2022, having failed to secure enough Democratic support. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for AB 1400.)

SB 42 (2025–2026), the California Fair Elections Act of 2026: Kalra was one of five Assembly principal coauthors (with Berman, Lee, and Pellerin among Assembly members, alongside Senate lead authors Umberg, Allen, and Cervantes). The Senate concurred in Assembly amendments 29–8 on September 13, 2025, and Gov. Gavin Newsom signed it October 2, 2025 as Chapter 245, Statutes of 2025, placing the measure before voters as Proposition 4 on the November 2026 ballot. Full detail on the measure itself is covered in content/measures/ca-prop-4-2026.json and is not duplicated here. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 42.)
attendance: No individually published floor-attendance or voting-participation record for Assemblymember Kalra was found. The California State Assembly does not publish a per-member attendance scorecard; the only public records are bill-by-bill roll-call votes at leginfo.legislature.ca.gov, which is what the voting-record entries above are drawn from. Third-party trackers such as CalMatters' Digital Democracy publish bill-passage counts and interest-group vote-alignment percentages for legislators but likewise do not publish an attendance metric; a search did not locate a Digital Democracy profile confirmed for Kalra at the time of writing.
